newsitem.title: VATICAN: Popes urges easing of sanctions in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: Popes urges easing of sanctions in Burundi.

text.p: Pope John Paul on Wednesday said he hoped international sanctions on Burundi would be eased, saying they were increasing the burden on a suffering people.
He made his remarks at the end of his weekly general audience in a renewed tribute to Archbishop Joachim Ruhuna, the country's senior Roman Catholic prelate, who died in an ambush on September 9.

"It is precisely in remembering him that I appreciate the initiatives of those who are working for a peaceful end to the divisions and I also share the suffering of all citizens which has now been increased by the sanctions in place.
"While I invite you to pray for peace, I hope that these sanctions, which are creating a greater burden for the civilian population, will be eased," the Pope said.
The Vatican opposes economic sanctions on principle, arguing that they hit civilians hardest.
East African countries slapped the boycott on landlocked Burundi after Tutsi military ruler Pierre Buyoya took power in a coup on July 25.
His Prime Minister Pascal Firmin Ndimira said on Tuesday that the sanctions were helping extremists in the conflict between minority Tutsis and majority Hutus.

Officials from East African countries were expected to meet in neighbouring Rwanda on Wednesday to discuss the blockade which cut off Burundi's oil imports and exports of coffee, the main cash earner.
Around 150,000 people, mainly civilians, have been killed in violence since a failed coup in which Burundi's first democratically elected president was killed in October 1993.
